tools_used: WebFetch (supremecourt.gov docket PDFs and docket pages)
helpful: Snapshot docket links to the BIO and reply PDFs, which let me read the opposition the provisioning step had not fetched
sal-v4 segment table with bracketed reached rates per Term, directly poolable for the anchor
Full petition text and QP file
gaps: documents.json was fetched before the BIOs and reply existed; a re-fetch at provisioning time (or a cutoff-aware refresh) would have provisioned them
No statpack cut for petitions where a response was requested after waiver; the CFR is the strongest as-at signal on this docket and I had to price it from outside literature
fedcourts query has no caption or subject search, so it cannot find sibling petitions (same counsel, same theory) that were the decisive evidence here
CourtListener MCP shared rate limit (300/hour) was already exhausted on my first call
notes: WebFetch's summarizer cannot read PDF binaries; it saved them to disk and I extracted the text with pypdf via uv run --with. A built-in PDF-to-text step for docket links would remove that detour.
